cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations, Mum. Come with me; I'll introduce the winner before you thank the judges.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your cake isn't on the judging table. Where is it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In the kitchen, where I can admire it privately. You may inspect it after we've celebrated yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You withdrew so I'd win. I won't give a speech accepting a favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then thank the judges for choosing between eight cakes. I'll name the field, and you tell them about yours. Seven people entered to win; they deserve to hear from the person who beat them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls award introduction, A3 defers B2 inspection until celebration, A5 directs B4 refused speech toward real competitors; authority shapes protection of Mum confidence while withdrawal motive stays hidden.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing cake causes A3 private admiration; B4 favor-speech refusal causes A5 eight-cake field and winner contribution.

relationship.evidence: B2 notices A absence and B4 refuses false praise, a credible winner wanting deserved recognition.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 objection to emphasize seven actual opponents in the speech, giving a reason to accept the public role without revealing A concession.

specificity.evidence: A1 Mum winner, judging table and awards thanks establish family and contest; A5 field count is introduced by A as known context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 others deserve hearing from their winner is an earned protective redirection, different from the chess photograph tactic.

coach2.inferred: A protects confidence by excluding A nonentry from the comparison; it does not prove Mum would beat A.
coach2.missing: No essential missing fact; exact eight count is a newly spoken contest detail, not an invented reviewer backstory.
coach2.firstDefect: No blocking defect after changing the duplicate photo tactic.
